state.title: Replace the use of private `monkeypatch` fixture API
state.description:
Replace the use of private `monkeypatch` API with the standard invocations to fix compatibility with pytest 9.1, as well as to make the tests more reliable in the future.

The previous code operated on `monkeypatch` fixture internals to trigger clearing environment variables expected by tests at the beginning of tests, and reverting any changes made by the tests.  However, this does not seem strictly valid, and it actually lead to tests making wrong assumptions.  For example, `test_disable_dotenv_from_env` relied on a previous test unsetting `FOO` in the environment, and failed if `FOO` was set while it was run alone.

The new logic uses public API only: it cleans up the standard set of environment variables for every test, and additionally cleans up variables specifically used by dotenv tests.  With this approach, it is entirely possible for a test to leave the environment "dirty"; however, that's fine since other tests need to clean up the environment anyway to account for user-set environment variables.

Fixes #6071

state.scope: PR metadata and complete diff only; no full repository checkout, linked issue bodies, inline review threads, CI logs or locally executed upstream tests.

value.instructions: Choose the value category under the fixed criteria. Small changes can be meaningful. Dependency/release maintenance is valuable but distinct from a substantive fix. Do not use approval or popularity as evidence.

criteria.substantive: A concrete functional, security, documentation correctness or test-quality benefit beyond routine upkeep is supported by the description and diff. A dependency bump fixing a specific reported failure qualifies. This assesses purpose, not proof of runtime correctness.
criteria.routine_maintenance: Legitimate upkeep such as routine dependency pins or release metadata, without a specific project failure fixed by the diff. Not meaningless; upstream changelog features alone do not turn a routine pin bump into a project feature.
criteria.no_clear_value: The supplied evidence shows the change to be redundant, ineffective or purely churn, with no identifiable project benefit.
criteria.insufficient_evidence: The supplied material is missing or contradictory enough that even intended project value cannot be assessed.
